title: The Higher Price Is Erased by the Longer Voyage
subtitle: Thermal coal firmed to 107 dollars a ton as Turkish buyers chased cargo, but rerouting to the Baltic costs exporters 15 to 30 dollars a ton.

source.name: Seaborne thermal coal price assessments and Russian export freight economics

data.label: Coal price, CIF
data.annotation: Up 3.6% in the week as Turkish demand ran into sold-out southern port stocks.

data.label: Baltic rerouting penalty
data.annotation: Longer voyages and slower ship turnover erode the netback per ton.

primaryMetric.label: of the headline price consumed by rerouting

supportingFacts.label: Russian coal Turkish buyers may need over the next three months but cannot currently buy.
A coal carrier was struck in the Black Sea, pushing buyers towards Baltic cargo and rail through Azerbaijan.

metadata.keyFinding: Rerouting to the Baltic costs up to 30 dollars a ton against a 107 dollar price.
